report.source_text: Three weeks later, the patient showed subjective and objective improvement in ocular symptoms. Visual acuity improved to 20/20 bilaterally, with normal IOP. Slit lamp examination revealed clear and unremarkable anterior segments bilaterally. Mild lower vitritis (0.5 + cells) was found in both eyes. Fundus examination revealed mild elevation and slight blurring of the nasal optic disc bilaterally. In the right eye, the macula appeared dry with two small, pinpoint, paracentral well-defined hypopigmented foci and no signs of inflammation in the peripheral retina. In the left eye, a dry macula with a small hypopigmented focus was located nasally to the fovea, and there was no inflammation on the periphery.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male soldier presented with bilateral ocular inflammation (paracentral scotoma, scattered dark spots) and systemic symptoms including fever, headaches, night sweats, rash, and significant weight loss. Initial ophthalmological examination revealed bilateral retinitis and mild optic disc blurriness. Laboratory investigations showed thrombocytosis, elevated atypical lymphocytes, elevated liver enzymes, and an elevated ESR. Serological testing for infectious causes was positive for Rickettsia typhi, while negative for toxoplasmosis and syphilis. Based on these findings, Rickettsia typhi infection was diagnosed. Treatment with doxycycline and prednisone was initiated, leading to significant subjective and objective improvement in ocular symptoms, visual acuity, and resolution of inflammation within three weeks.

Fundus examination revealed bilateral mild elevation and blurriness of the optic discs nasally, and yellowish foci consistent with retinitis in both maculae.
Laboratory investigations revealed thrombocytosis, elevated atypical lymphocyte count, elevated liver enzymes, and an elevated ESR of 24 mm/hr.
Serological testing was positive for Rickettsia typhi, and negative for toxoplasmosis and syphilis.
Treatment consisted of doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and prednisone 50 mg daily.

Three weeks post-treatment, the patient showed subjective and objective improvement in ocular symptoms, with visual acuity improving to 20/20 bilaterally, normal IOP, clear anterior segments, and mild lower vitritis.
